recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: Sleep averaging only 4.2h/night (vs baseline 4.4h); 14/14 nights <7h in last 14 days
Training readiness score at 17 (7-day avg: 31.4), well below functional threshold
Recovery balance is +1.96 but acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR) is 0.7 — indicating under-recovery *and* under-training, not balanced recovery
HRV is elevated (+4.6% vs baseline), which often reflects parasympathetic dominance due to fatigue or insufficient stimulus, not robust recovery
readiness.guidance: This athlete is not recovered enough for quality training; the priority this week is restoring sleep and re-establishing autonomic resilience — not adding load.

monthly_review.summary: Pace improved significantly this month (519 → 539 sec/km), but volume dropped (55.8 → 61.0 km), cadence declined (146 → 151 spm), and efficiency worsened (13.62 → 13.46 ml O2/kg/km), suggesting fatigue or pacing inconsistency rather than fitness gain.
monthly_review.highlight: The 20-sec/km pace improvement occurred alongside higher average HR (+3 bpm), lower cadence (-5 spm), and elevated aerobic TE (+0.3), indicating inefficient effort — consistent with accumulated fatigue rather than true performance gain, and confirmed by the 3-month trend showing no sustained pace improvement (May: 551, April: 532, March: 534).

goal_tracker.message: 5.2 km across up to 3 sessions remain to match last month’s volume — but given compromised readiness (sleep debt, low training readiness score of 17, and chronic under-recovery), chasing this number would risk further fatigue accumulation and is not advisable; prioritizing rest and sleep restoration is the correct call.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt directly correlates with worsening running economy
insights.body: Sleep averaged 4.2h/night (14/14 nights <7h) while recent running economy spiked to 262.2 ml O2/kg/km — the highest in the 6-run recent series and 3.5% above rolling median (253.9), confirming literature linking sub-6h sleep with ~3–5% RE deterioration.

insights.title: Low ACWR masks aerobic fragility
insights.body: ACWR is 0.7 (‘LOW’ status), yet aerobic decoupling median is 6.66% (well above 5% threshold), and latest decoupling is only 0.84% — a single outlier likely from low-intensity effort (HR 141, pace 9:15/km on 14.1 km), not systemic aerobic resilience.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominates despite declining VO2max responsiveness
insights.body: Zone 3 comprises 26% of July volume (up from 19% in May), yet VO2max remains flat at 39.0 (baseline 36.2, delta +2.9), and per-zone efficiency drops sharply in Z3 (0.7508 m/beat) vs Z2 (0.7891), suggesting disproportionate time spent in 'gray zone' without commensurate adaptation.

insights.title: Stride length variability signals neuromuscular fatigue
insights.body: Stride length swings from 70.36 cm (14.1 km long run) to 89.8 cm (0.9 km recovery jog) — a 27% range — while vertical oscillation stays stable (7.5–8.5 cm), implying compensatory mechanics likely driven by sleep-deprived motor control.

recommendations.action: Prioritize sleep: target ≥6.5 hours nightly for all 7 days; use body battery as proxy — stop all screen time by 21:00 and implement 10-min guided breathwork before bed.
recommendations.reason: Sleep is the most suppressed recovery metric (4.2h avg, 14/14 nights <7h) and directly drives HRV, efficiency, and decoupling outcomes.

recommendations.action: One 30-min Zone 1 walk or very easy jog (HR ≤120 bpm, pace >10:30/km) on Wednesday — no distance target, only perceived exertion ≤2/10.
recommendations.reason: Resting HR has dropped (-1.4 bpm), confirming parasympathetic engagement is possible, but training readiness is critically low (17/100); this maintains rhythm without stress.

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 3+ efforts for 7 days; replace planned intervals or tempo with Zone 2 only if HR stays ≤135 bpm and aerobic TE remains ≤2.8.
recommendations.reason: Zone 3 volume is high (26%) yet efficiency in Z3 is lowest among zones (0.7508 m/beat), and decoupling median suggests underlying aerobic inefficiency — pushing intensity now risks reinforcing poor economy.

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep deprivation increasing injury susceptibility
risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep in last 14 days; vertical oscillation increased to 8.5 cm (vs 7.5 cm in March), indicating reduced neuromuscular control
risk_flags.action: Enforce strict sleep hygiene for 7 days before reassessing stride metrics.

risk_flags.risk: Autonomic imbalance masked by elevated HRV
risk_flags.evidence: HRV is +4.6% above baseline but resting HR dropped -1.4 bpm *and* training readiness is 17 — classic sign of 'fatigue-induced vagal dominance', not health
risk_flags.action: Pause all HR-based intensity targets for 7 days; rely solely on RPE and breathing ease.

risk_flags.risk: Gray-zone training entrenching inefficient movement patterns
risk_flags.evidence: Zone 3 accounts for 26% of July volume, yet efficiency in Z3 (0.7508 m/beat) is lowest across zones and stride length varies 27% across recent runs
risk_flags.action: Replace all Zone 3 sessions with Zone 2 (HR ≤135) or Zone 1 until aerobic decoupling median falls below 5% for 3 consecutive runs.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational recovery rhythms by prioritizing sleep consistency and eliminating gray-zone effort — allowing HRV, stride stability, and aerobic decoupling to recalibrate before reintroducing structure.
suggested_sessions: Complete rest with sleep audit (track bedtime/waketime, no screens after 21:00)
